about: The bean splitter's vectors: bin/parse.py split_front_matter, which a port elsewhere is held to as well. Each case is a document's text and how it splits: its front matter (null where it is not fenced) and its body. Run by test/core_read.py.

cases.name: a bean: the front matter keeps the line break after the first fence, the body the one after the second
a byte-order mark before the first fence is let go
a byte-order mark at the start of a document with no fence is let go too: not fenced, the rest the body
a byte-order mark before an opening fence with no closing one is let go: not fenced, the rest the body
line ends CR LF: a fence takes the CR before its LF, and the lines between keep theirs
a rule in the body is the body's: only the first two fences split
no fence: not fenced, the text whole as the body
a fence may end in spaces or tabs
an opening fence and no closing one: not fenced
the first fence is the first line, or the document is not fenced
a fence does not begin with a space
a fence is the whole line: three dashes and a word are text
the closing fence at the very end: an empty body
a byte-order mark after the start is text, kept where it is
a line ended by CR alone ends no line: not fenced
a line separator (U+2028) ends no line: not fenced
a fence after a line separator is no fence: only LF begins a line
